result.title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
result.summary: Despite strong performance on standard benchmarks, video reasoning models remain vulnerable to visual degradation, raising concerns about their reliability in safety-critical scenarios. Existing benchmarks address this concern in part by simulating visual degradation or probing model reasoning with challenging questions, leaving open how well models handle naturally degraded video and whether they can make the simpler judgments that matter for safe driving. To this end, we introduce GRAPE-Bench, which jointly evaluates video reasoning across visual degradation conditions and question difficulty. It combines a synthetic set spanning twelve corruption types across daily-life and driving videos with real-world footage of driving at night or in rain, snow, or fog. Each video is paired with three progressively challenging questions, from fundamental judgments with potential safety implications to demanding reasoning stress tests. Across open-weight and frontier models, we observe ranking reversals between synthetic and real-world conditions and level-specific weaknesses obscured by overall accuracy. Synthetic-data fine-tuning improves Qwen3.5-9B's real-world accuracy from 76.7% to 81.1%, while clean-privileged on-policy distillation reaches 80.4% in a separate reasoning-enabled setting. Through preference steering, we further demonstrate continuous control over a frozen model's trade-off between safety-relevant judgments and challenging reasoning, with little change in overall accuracy. Together, GRAPE-Bench provides a unified testbed for evaluating, improving, and controlling video reasoning under degraded visual conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GRAPE-Bench，把视觉退化条件与问题难度联合纳入视频推理评测：合成十二类损坏加入夜、雨雪雾真实驾驶视频，每题配三级递进问题，测试开放权重与前沿模型，并尝试合成数据微调与偏好引导。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准为视觉证据受损时的多模态推理提供诊断与失败分析，可供核查模型是否真正使用视觉细节、以及安全相关简单判断的薄弱环节；其偏好引导对「安全判断与高难推理」权衡的连续调控，可能为视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供线索。
